exposure: Advanced Skilled Birth Attendant (ASBA) task-shifting initiative
presence of family physician or another ASBA
outcome: performance of Cesarean sections by ASBA graduates
reasons for non-performance of Cesarean sections
reduced burden of Cesarean sections on staff
expansion of life-saving surgical care provision
improved working conditions in rural hospitals
cohort: The study participants included Advanced Skilled Birth Attendant (ASBA) graduates and staff from rural government hospitals employing ASBA graduates in Nepal.
finding: The ASBA program successfully reduces human resource shortages, expands the provision of life-saving Cesarean section, and improves the working conditions in rural hospitals within the LMIC setting.
mod_finding: The ASBA program successfully expands the provision of life-saving Cesarean sections by trained medical officers in rural hospitals.
cross-section timing: Data was collected on ASBA graduates' performance and perceptions immediately after training and at the time of the study ('today').
